properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 6:59PM MDT until October 24 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte,.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.5 feet, Moderate Flood. Water flows over low spots
in Hanna Lane Road west of Del Norte. Water threatens homes and RV
park near Del Norte Park in Del Norte. Homes near First Street and
the Oak Street Bridge on Colorado Highway 112 are threatened by
high water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:46 PM MDT Friday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:46 PM MDT Friday was 6.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 3.0 feet early Wednesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.4
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 700 AM MDT.

properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Los Alamos County in north central New Mexico...
South Central Rio Arriba County in north central New Mexico...
Northeastern Sandoval County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 745 PM MDT.

* At 658 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles east of
Fenton Lake State Park, or 18 miles west of Los Alamos, moving
northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Los Alamos, Abiquiu and Santa Clara Pueblo.
properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the
Rio Grande River and waterways downstream.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone will continue until the water has a chance to
recede. Several roads remain closed due to flooding...including
highway 160 and Park Creek Road due to a washed out bridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 649 PM MDT, Stream gauges indicate flooding continues for the
South Fork Rio Grande, Rio Grande between South Fork and Del
Norte, and other area streams and waterways.
- The South Fork Rio Grande and other area streams are past their
crests and are continuing to fall. The South Fork Rio Grande is
expected to fall back below Flood Stage late tonight.

The Rio Grande River and its tributaries including the South Fork
area and along highway 160 to Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

unstable and unsafe.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This is the flood of record.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Friday the stage was 14.1 feet. Thereafter, the
river gage was no longer operational. The river is likely near
crest as of 6:00 PM MDT.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Friday was 14.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Saturday afternoon and continue falling to 3.2 feet Wednesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.3
feet on 09/06/1909.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Cibola, NM; McKinley, NM; Sandoval, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 23 at 6:38PM MDT until October 23 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 638 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated the heaviest rainfall has
exited the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of rain fell in
the past two hours on top of saturated soils. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marquez, Cebolletita, Seboyeta, Bibo, Paguate and Encinal.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Seboyetita Creek, Salado Creek, San Miguel Creek, and Canada Ancha.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Conejos, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 6:38PM MDT until October 23 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and other area streams
caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Western Conejos County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, area streams, and other
low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected to continue.
Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. Flooded waterways
will continue to run high into the late evening hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 633 PM MDT, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area though amounts will be spotty in coverage.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cumbres Pass and Platoro.
- Highway 17 between Antonito and Cumbres Pass remains closed.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Otero County in south central New Mexico...
North Central El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 930 PM MDT.

* At 632 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Northeast El Paso, Chaparral, Fort Bliss, Fort Bliss Northeast and
Biggs Field.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 6:20PM MDT until October 23 at 9:15PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...
Central Sierra County in south central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 620 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall of up to 0.5 inches is expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Upham, Arrey, Caballo, Derry, Engle, Cutter, Spaceport America,
Elephant Butte Lake and Caballo Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
